messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: CFLAGS inconsistent in makefiles
parts:
Hi!

As we are currently updating the make system I noticed that we had all the time different CFLAGS definitions in the makefiles,i.e.:

math:
CFLAGS = -I . -isystem $(EIGEN) -isystem $(BOOST) -Wall -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS -DNO_FPRINTF_OUTPUT -pipe -I$(CVODE)/include

stan and cmdstan:
CFLAGS = -I . -isystem $(EIGEN) -isystem $(BOOST) -Wall -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS -pipe -I$(CVODE)/include


That is, only the math repo had the -DNO_FPRINTF_OUTPUT flag. Should this possibly be aligned?

Sebastian

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] CFLAGS inconsistent in makefiles
parts:
> On Apr 17, 2016, at 5:06 AM, Sebastian Weber <sdw....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I saw that you already got the 32bit windows fix to cmdstan and stan. I added the printf stuff.
>
> I was wondering if we could have a single place where these make includes are? Maybe in math and then the others point there? I am not too familiar with the git stuff, but I saw that Ben did something like this in rstan, so maybe we could use this here as well.

I was thinking about that yesterday. There might be a way to do it if we moved most of the logic into math.

The hard part is working through the edge cases when submodules haven't been updated or on Windows.

I haven't paid much attention since it hasn't been too much of a maintenance burden. My guess is after these pull requests, we won't change the makefile a for months.

>
> This double maintenance with issue+pull requests is quite a lot of work.

Agreed, but I think it's the right thing to do. It does a few things for us:
- writing release notes is much easier; if you want a comparison, look at closed pull requests vs closed issues
- issues are where we specify the issue
- pull requests are proposed fixes. Not every pull request will go in. Sometimes design or implementation is off and pull requests get closed when the issue stays open

With that said, if it is too much of a burden on us all, I'm happy if we streamline our process. I prefer shorter to longer process.

>
> Sebastian

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] CFLAGS inconsistent in makefiles
parts:
Hi Daniel,

First, I think the issue+pull approach is great for most stuff! Still, I find myself not fixing one-liners just due to the hassle of going through the process. So maybe a process for "small" fixes could be added to the processes. Here are two ideas:

1. We all agree that leaving those templates which we have in most parts empty if a change is small is ok.

2. Each developer keeps an open branch for small fixes. Each commit to that branch must only be a small change and should be accompanied by a descriptive commit message. Once the developer reaches a threshold (maybe 5) of such small commits, he creates an issue+pull which lists those small changes.

Finally, we would need to define what "small" is. One-liners, removing compiler warnings, etc. ... needs to be defined on a wiki.

I think this would help to make small changes go in quicker.

Just an idea.

Sebastian
